title: Bayes Theorem Calculator
description: Compute posterior probabilities from prior, sensitivity and specificity with the full Bayes formula, natural frequencies and a probability tree.
howto: Enter the prior probability P(D) — how common the condition is.
Enter the test's sensitivity P(+|D) and specificity P(−|¬D).
Press Calculate to get P(D|+) and P(D|−) with every formula step.
Read the natural-frequency view (per 10,000 people) to build intuition.

faqs.a: P(D|+) = P(+|D)·P(D) / P(+), where P(+) = P(+|D)·P(D) + P(+|¬D)·P(¬D). It updates the prior probability with the evidence from the test result.

faqs.q: Why can P(D|+) be low even with a 99% accurate test?
faqs.a: The base-rate effect: if the condition is rare, most positives come from the large healthy group, so false positives dominate. The natural-frequency table makes this visible.

faqs.q: What do sensitivity and specificity mean?
faqs.a: Sensitivity is P(positive | has condition) — the true positive rate. Specificity is P(negative | no condition) — the true negative rate.
